keyTerms.definition: The step that converts text to integer token IDs.
The fixed dictionary that maps text pieces to integers.
Byte pair encoding. It learns merge rules from a corpus.
The average number of tokens per word.
Out-of-vocabulary. A word missing from the vocabulary.

recall.question: Why do modern LLMs use subword tokenization instead of words?
recall.answer: Word vocabularies explode and leave unknown words. Subwords split rare words into reusable pieces, so every string decomposes into known pieces.

recall.question: What are the two phases of BPE?
recall.answer: Training learns merge rules from a corpus. Encoding applies the rules greedily in learned order.

recall.question: Why does fertility matter in practice?
recall.answer: Providers count context windows and prices in tokens. High fertility means fewer words fit and costs rise.

sections.title: Embeddings: points in a learned space

keyTerms.definition: A learned vector of floats that stands for one token.
The lookup table with one row per vocabulary entry.
A vector with 1 at one position and 0 elsewhere.
Reusing one matrix for input and output embeddings.

recall.question: What does distance between embeddings mean?
recall.answer: Similarity. Tokens with nearby points get similar treatment from the network.

recall.question: Why are learned embeddings better than one-hot?
recall.answer: One-hot makes every token equally far from every other token. Learned vectors turn similarity into geometry.

recall.question: What is the context-free limitation of embeddings?
recall.answer: The token bank gets the same vector in river bank and bank loan. Attention builds meaning in context later.

keyTerms.definition: Differentiable retrieval over a sequence.
The function that turns scores into weights that sum to one.
The rule that stops a token from peeking at the future.
Dividing by sqrt(d_k) to keep softmax out of saturation.

recall.question: What are the five steps of one attention head?
recall.answer: Project to Q, K, V. Score with QK^T over sqrt(d_k). Apply the causal mask. Apply softmax. Mix the values.

recall.question: Why does attention scale by sqrt(d_k)?
recall.answer: It keeps softmax out of saturation so gradients flow.

recall.question: What is the cost of attention?
recall.answer: O(n^2 d) time and O(n^2) memory. At 4k context, one head's score matrix is 67 MB.

keyTerms.definition: The signal that gives attention a sense of order.
Fixed multi-frequency waves used as position codes.
Rotary position embedding. It rotates Q and K by position.
The gap n minus m, which RoPE makes scores depend on.

recall.question: Why does attention need positional encodings?
recall.answer: Attention is permutation-invariant. Without them it cannot see order.

recall.question: What does RoPE do to Q and K?
recall.answer: It rotates them by position-proportional angles. Scores then depend only on relative distance.

recall.question: Where must you never apply RoPE?
recall.answer: To V. Apply it to Q and K only.

keyTerms.definition: A smooth ReLU-like gate that uses the Gaussian CDF.
A learned gate. It multiplies Swish(xW) by xV.
LayerNorm without mean centering.
Placing normalization before the sublayer in the block.

recall.question: Why did pre-norm win?
recall.answer: The residual path stays unnormalized, so gradients flow through deep stacks.

recall.question: What is SwiGLU?
recall.answer: A learned gate. It multiplies Swish(xW) by xV and uses three MLP matrices. It is the modern default.

recall.question: How does RMSNorm differ from LayerNorm?
recall.answer: It skips mean centering. It is cheaper and equally stabilizing.

sections.title: Multi-head attention and the transformer block

keyTerms.definition: Several independent attention distributions in parallel subspaces.
The shared workspace that sublayers add deltas to.
The per-position feedforward network in each block.

recall.question: What does one transformer block do, in order?
recall.answer: Pre-norm, attention, residual add, pre-norm, MLP, residual add.

recall.question: What mixes across positions, and what computes per position?
recall.answer: Attention mixes across positions. The MLP computes per position.

recall.question: Where do most block parameters live?
recall.answer: In the MLP, about three times the parameters of attention.

keyTerms.definition: Multi-head attention. It uses h key-value heads.
Multi-query attention. It uses one shared key-value head.
Grouped-query attention. It uses g groups of key-value heads.
Stored keys and values reused across decode steps.

recall.question: What shrinks from MHA to MQA to GQA?
recall.answer: Only the K and V heads shrink. Query heads never shrink.

recall.question: What is the KV cache formula per token?
recall.answer: 2 times layers times KV-heads times head-dim times bytes.

recall.question: Why does GQA-8 speed up generation?
recall.answer: Fewer KV heads mean less memory bandwidth per decode step.

keyTerms.definition: The compute-bound first pass over the prompt.
The memory-bandwidth-bound token-by-token phase.
Stored keys and values reused across decode steps.
The latency metric for prefill.

recall.question: What does the KV cache store, and what is never cached?
recall.answer: It stores past K and V per layer. Q is never cached.

recall.question: Why is decode memory-bandwidth bound?
recall.answer: Each step appends one token's K and V and reuses the rest. Bandwidth limits speed, not compute.

recall.question: What does the cache cap in serving?
recall.answer: Batch size. Context length becomes a serving cost.

keyTerms.definition: Rebuilding a result exactly to prove understanding.
Dealing with words never seen in training.
The numerical library used for the attention lab.

recall.question: What does Lab A prove?
recall.answer: Your attention implementation matches the hand-computed numbers from Chapter 3.

recall.question: What does Lab B prove?
recall.answer: Your BPE trainer reproduces the merge sequence, then handles unseen words.

recall.question: Your numbers disagree with the chapter. What does it mean?
recall.answer: Your implementation has a bug. It is not a rounding choice.

keyTerms.definition: Dividing positions by s to fit a longer context.
Raising the RoPE base to protect high frequencies.
Per-dimension ramps plus a temperature fix for long context.
Early tokens that keep attracting attention mass.

recall.question: Why does RoPE break past its training length?
recall.answer: The angles are unfamiliar. Extension methods make long positions look familiar again.

recall.question: What does NTK-aware scaling do?
recall.answer: It raises the base to b times s^(D/(D-2)) and protects high frequencies. It often works with no fine-tuning at 2x to 4x.

recall.question: When is YaRN the right recipe?
recall.answer: When you plan to fine-tune for long context.
